hindi: गायत्र के गायक तुम्हें गाते हैं; स्तुति करने वाले अर्क (स्तुतिगान) से तुम्हारी स्तुति करते हैं; हे शतक्रतो, ब्राह्मण पुरोहितों ने तुम्हें बाँस की बल्ली की तरह ऊपर उठाया है।
english: The singers of the gāyatra sing to you; the praisers praise you with the song of praise (arka); the priests (brahmans) have raised you up, O hundred-powered one, like a pole.
notes: śatakrata is the vocative śatakrato with Vedic -o > -a before the following vowel (hiatus). The simile 'like a pole' (udvaṃśam iva) is taken literally; its exact point is not explained by the text. 'arcanti arkam' is taken as 'praise with the arka'.

words.gloss: true lord, lord of the true

hindi: सब स्तुतियों ने इन्द्र को बढ़ाया है, जो समुद्र के समान विस्तार वाला है, रथियों में सबसे श्रेष्ठ रथी है, वाजों (पुरस्कारों) का सच्चा स्वामी, स्वामी है।
english: All the songs have strengthened Indra, who is wide as the ocean, the best charioteer of charioteers, the true lord of prizes, the lord.
notes: 'samudra-vyacasam' is taken as 'having the expanse of the ocean'. 'satpatim' could also be 'lord of the good (sat)'. vājānām: 'prizes' (vāja also 'strength').

hindi: हे इन्द्र, इस निचोड़े हुए, सबसे श्रेष्ठ, अमर आनन्ददायक रस को पियो; उज्ज्वल सोम की धाराएँ ऋत के आसन पर तुम्हारी ओर बही हैं।
english: O Indra, drink this pressed, supreme, immortal exhilarating draught; the streams of the bright juice have flowed to you in the seat of order (ṛta).
notes: śukrasya is taken with the unstated 'juice/Soma'. 'Seat of ṛta' is kept literal.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हे अद्भुत, हे पत्थर के धारी, जो कुछ तुम्हारा दिया हुआ यहाँ मेरे पास नहीं है, हे धन पाने वाले, वह धन हमारे लिए दोनों हाथों से लाओ।
english: O Indra, wonderful one, whatever given by you is not here with me, O wielder of the stone, that bounty bring to us, O finder of wealth, with both hands.
notes: 'ubhayāhastyā' is read as ubhayā hastyā ā (padapāṭha-style); the form hastyā is uncertain (instrumental of hastya 'hand-ful', or the compound ubhayāhasti); sense 'with both hands' is kept. 'tvādātam' = tvā-dātam 'given by you' (tvā for tvayā); vidadvaso 'finder/winner of wealth' (not the glossary vaso).

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तिरश्ची की पुकार सुनो, जो तुम्हारी सेवा करता है; उत्तम वीर्य से युक्त और गायों वाला धन देकर हमें भर दो, क्योंकि तुम महान हो।
english: Hear the call of Tiraścī, O Indra, who serves you; fill us with wealth rich in cattle and good heroic strength, for you are great.

text_flags.why: possible: printed d for dh; the usual imperative of √śru is śrudhī (Rigvedic śrudhī havam)

notes: tiraścyāḥ is taken as the genitive of the name Tiraścī (a seer), by analogy with the Ṛgvedic parallel; 'of the one who goes athwart' is an alternative. The object of pūrdhi ('us') is not in the text; suvīryasya gomataḥ is taken loosely as describing the wealth.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हे सबसे बलवान, तुम्हारे लिए सोम निचोड़ा गया है; हे साहसी, आओ। इन्द्रिय-बल तुम्हें भर दे, जैसे सूर्य अपनी किरणों से अन्तरिक्ष को भर देता है।
english: Soma has been pressed for you, O Indra, most mighty; come, bold one. May vigour fill you, as the sun fills the space with his rays.
notes: dhṛṣṇavā is taken as dhṛṣṇo ā (o + ā > avā). In the last line the syntax of tvā, indriyam and rajaḥ is ambiguous (what fills what); the translation takes 'may power fill you, as the sun (fills) the space with rays'.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, अपने हरे घोड़ों के साथ कण्व की सुन्दर स्तुति के पास आओ; उस शासन करते हुए द्युलोक से, हे दिवावसु, द्युलोक की ओर जाओ।
english: Come here, O Indra, with your bay horses to the good praise of Kaṇva; from yonder ruling heaven go to heaven, O Divāvasu.
notes: Doubtful unit. divo amuṣya śāsato is taken as 'of that heaven which rules'; divam yaya as 'go to heaven' (yaya read as a Vedic imperative of √yā); divāvaso is taken as an epithet 'whose wealth is the day/heaven' or a proper name (Divāvasu). The relation of the two clauses is unclear; the translation is tentative.

hindi: हे स्तुतिप्रिय, सोम निचोड़े जाने पर स्तुतियाँ रथी की तरह तुम्हारे पास आ खड़ी हुई हैं; जैसे दुधारू गायें बछड़े को पुकारती हैं, वैसे ही वे तुम्हें पुकारती हैं।
english: Our songs have come to stand by you at the pressings, O lover of songs, like a charioteer; they cry out to you as milch cows to a calf.
notes: 'ā ... asthuḥ' is rendered 'have come to stand by'. 'sam-anūṣata' is taken from √nū 'cry, sound'.

hindi: आओ, अब हम शुद्ध इन्द्र की शुद्ध साम से स्तुति करें; शुद्ध उक्थों से बढ़े हुए (इन्द्र) की; दूध के मिश्रण वाला वह शुद्ध (पदार्थों) से आनन्दित हो।
english: Come, let us now praise Indra, the pure one, with a pure chant (sāman), him who has grown strong through pure hymns; may he, possessing the milk-mixture, rejoice with pure (offerings).
notes: The last pāda is ambiguous: 'śuddhaiḥ' has no stated noun (offerings/praises); the subject of mamattu (Indra or the Soma) is taken as Indra. 'eto' = eta u. Verse 387 begins with the same words.

hindi: जो धन में सबसे धनी है, जो तेजों में सबसे तेजस्वी है, वह निचोड़ा हुआ सोम, हे इन्द्र, हे स्वधा के स्वामी, तुम्हारे लिए आनन्ददायक रस है।
english: The Soma that is the richest in wealth and the most splendid in splendours has been pressed; it is for you, O Indra, lord of svadhā, the exhilarating draught.

text_flags.why: possible: the Ṛgvedic parallel reads rayivaḥ (voc.) rayintamaḥ; printed rayiṃ vo may be a variant or a different word division

notes: Read as printed, rayiṃ vo would be 'wealth ... of/for you (pl.)', which fits poorly with the singular address te/indra; so it is taken as rayi-vaḥ. 'svadhā' left as svadhā (own power / sacrificial offering).

words.gram: m. dat. sg., bahuvrīhi, see notes

hindi: जो पीना चाहता है, जो जानने वाला है, शीघ्र पहुँचने वाला है, आने वाला है और पीछे न रहने वाला है, उसके लिए हे मनुष्यो, सब कुछ अर्पित करो।
english: To him who wishes to drink, to the knowing one, to him who readily goes, who comes, who does not lag behind, offer all things in return, O men.
notes: Doubtful words: araṅgamāya ('readily going', from araṃ 'sufficiently, readily' + gam) and apaścādadhvane (taken as a-paścāt-adhvan 'whose course is not behind'). The unstated subject (Indra) is supplied by the translation as 'him'. The addressee of bhara is taken as the plural 'naraḥ' (bhara is singular: 'bring!'), so the sense is loosely 'bring, O men'.

hindi: हमारे लिए... महान् को, गहरे में रहने वाले महान् को, पुरातन स्थान में रहने वाले को; तुमने उग्र वाणी को दूर हटा दिया है।
english: To us ... the great one lying in the nest (or in vigour), the great one dwelling in the deep, the great one dwelling in the ancient place; you have driven away the fierce speech.
notes: GROUPING: printed as a long first line (three eight-syllable pādas) plus a short second line; metrically it is four pādas of eight syllables, so the line division is unusual but the unit is a single verse. Doubtful throughout: 'vayovayaḥśayam' (vayaḥ vayaḥ-śayam?), 'gahvareṣṭhām' (gahvare-ṣṭhā 'abiding in the deep') and 'pūrvineṣṭhām' (not understood). The syntax of the first half is not clear (no verb), so the translation is only a literal sketch.

hindi: जैसे रथ को (घुमाकर लाते हैं) वैसे हम तुम्हें सहायता के लिए और कृपा के लिए इधर घुमाकर लाते हैं, हे सबसे बलवान इन्द्र, जो महाकर्मी है, आक्रमणों को जीतने वाला है और सत्य का स्वामी है।
english: We turn you hither for help and for favour, as (one turns) a chariot: Indra, mighty in deeds, overcoming onsets, O most mighty one, lord of the true.
notes: ṛtīṣaham is taken as 'overcoming assailants/onsets' (ṛtī); the sense is traditional but not certain. 'śaviṣṭha' is vocative though in apposition to the accusative Indra.

hindi: वह पुरातन, महान् जनों में सबसे आगे रहने वाला उत्सुक वेन अपने कर्मों से सुशोभित है; जिसके द्वारा पिता मनु देवों के बीच श्रद्धा से सम्मानित होता है।
english: He, the ancient one, the eager Vena of the great ones, is honoured by his deeds; through whom father Manu is honoured with devotion among the gods.
notes: The Ṛgvedic parallel reads mahānām; the printed mahonām is taken as the genitive plural of mahas 'great (ones)'. ānaje (twice) is taken as 'is anointed/honoured' (ā-√añj); dhiya is read as dhiyā. Sense uncertain: 'Vena' may also be read as the adjective 'longing, eager'; dvārā 'through (the door of) whom'.

hindi: जब तेज़ और चमकते हुए (वे) उसे रथों पर ढोते हैं, तो मादक मधु पीते हुए वे वहाँ यश प्राप्त करते हैं।
english: When the swift, shining ones carry him on the chariots, drinking the intoxicating sweet drink, there they win glories.
notes: The people referred to are not named in the unit. 'yadī' is taken as yad + ī 'when ... him'; 'ratheṣv ā' with ā as a particle 'on'.

hindi: मैं तुम्हारे लिए उस अजेय, बल के स्वामी की स्तुति करता हूँ: इन्द्र की, जो सबको जीतने वाला, वीर, सबसे समर्थ और सब कुछ जानने वाला है।
english: I praise for you that irresistible lord of strength: Indra, the all-conquering hero, the most able, the all-knowing.
notes: aprahaṇam: 'not to be struck down / irresistible'; viśvavedasam may also be 'possessing all wealth'. 'vaḥ' is the plural 'you', taken as 'for you'.

hindi: मैंने विजयी, वेगवान घोड़े दधिक्रावा का गुणगान किया है; वह हमारे मुखों को सुगन्धित करे और हमारी आयु को बढ़ाए।
english: I have celebrated Dadhikrāvan, the victorious, swift horse; may he make our mouths fragrant and prolong our lives.
notes: Dadhikrāvan is kept as a name; aśvasya 'of the horse' is in apposition.

hindi: किलों को तोड़ने वाला, युवा, कवि, अपार बल वाला (इन्द्र) उत्पन्न हुआ; इन्द्र, जो सारे कर्म का धारणकर्ता, वज्रधारी और बहुतों से स्तुत है।
english: The breaker of fortresses, young, a sage, of boundless might, was born: Indra, the upholder of every work, the wielder of the thunderbolt, much praised.
notes: dharttā is the spelling of dhartā with doubled t after r; no change in sense. bhindu is taken as an agent noun 'breaker'.

words.gloss: for the winning of the offering

hindi: आगे-आगे तुम्हारे लिए त्रिष्टुप् (स्तुति) और भोज्य अर्पित है, उस इन्दु (सोम-बिन्दु) के लिए जिसकी वीर वन्दना करते हैं; वह बुद्धि और उदारता से, यज्ञ-अन्न की प्राप्ति के लिए, तुम्हारी सेवा करता है।
english: Forth, forth for you the triṣṭubh (hymn) and the refreshment, for the drop (Indu) whom heroes praise; with insight and bounty he honours you for the winning of the offering.
notes: Doubtful. vandadvīrāya: either 'whom heroes praise' (vandat-vīra) or 'praising heroes'; the verb of the first line is not stated (supplied as 'is offered'); the subject of vivāsati (the drop? the singer?) is uncertain. medhasātaye 'for the winning of the offering/wisdom'.

words.gloss: finder of the light of heaven

hindi: काश्यप के, जो स्वर्ग का प्रकाश पाने वाले हैं, वे दोनों जिन्हें साथी (एक जुए में जुते हुए) कहा जाता है; जिन दोनों के सम्पूर्ण व्रत और यज्ञ को धीर जनों ने देखकर जाना है।
english: The two whom they call the companions of Kaśyapa, the finder of heaven's light, whose whole ordinance and sacrifice the wise have perceived.
notes: Doubtful: the unit has no main verb, and the two companions are not named in the text. Kaśyapa is kept as a name. 'sayujau iti' is taken as 'called yoke-fellows'. nicāyya 'having observed/perceived' (√ci, ni-cāyya).

hindi: गाओ, गाओ, हे पुरुषो; हे प्रियमेधो, गाओ; छोटे पुत्र भी गाएँ; और दुर्ग के प्रति निडर होकर गाओ।
english: Sing, sing forth, O men; sing, O Priyamedhas; let the little sons also sing, and sing boldly to the stronghold indeed.
notes: The Ṛgvedic parallel (8.69.8) reads puraṃ na dhṛṣṇu arcata ('sing boldly, like a stronghold'); the printed puram id is translated as given. dhṛṣṇu is taken as adverbial 'boldly'.

words.gloss: to him who drives off many

hindi: इन्द्र के लिए, बहुतों को हटाने वाले के लिए, बढ़ाने वाला और गाने योग्य उक्थ (स्तोत्र); जिससे शक्र हमारे सोम-अभिषवों में और मित्रताओं में आनन्दित हो।
english: A hymn to be recited, strengthening, for Indra, who drives off many; so that the mighty one (Śakra) may delight in us at the pressings and in friendships.
notes: rāraṇat: 'may he delight (in us)', with naḥ taken as 'in us'. puruniḥṣidhe 'who drives off/restrains many' is uncertain.

hindi: मैं सहायता के लिए पुकारता हूँ: विश्वानर के धन के स्वामी को, अटल बल वाले को; और जनों तथा रथों के मार्गों से भी।
english: I call for help the lord of wealth of Viśvānara (of all men), of unbowed strength, and (I call) with the courses of the peoples, of the chariots.
notes: Doubtful. 'viśvānarasya vaspatim' is read as viśvānarasya vasaḥ-patim 'the lord of wealth of Viśvānara'; viśvā-nara may be a name or 'of all men'. 'anānatasya śavasaḥ' is taken as genitive in apposition ('of unbowed strength'). evaiḥ (inst. pl. of eva 'course') is uncertain, as are the relations of the two genitives carṣaṇīnām and rathānām.

hindi: जो तुम्हारा द्युलोक का पुरुष है, मेहनत करने वाले मर्त्य की प्रार्थना से, सहायता द्वारा वह महान् द्युलोक के शत्रुओं और संकट को पार करता है।
english: He indeed who is your man of heaven, by the prayer of the toiling mortal, through help crosses over the hostilities and distress of great heaven.
notes: Doubtful. 'na' in 'aṃho na tarati' is left unresolved (it can be 'like' or 'not'; the translation does not render it). 'bṛhato divaḥ' is taken with the foes/distress ('of great heaven'); 'te divo naraḥ' is read as 'your man of heaven'. The sense of the whole verse is not secure.

words.gloss: O seeing all, lord of all peoples

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हे शतक्रतो, तुम्हारे प्रचुर दान की भेंट विपुल है; इसलिए हे सब मनुष्यों के द्रष्टा, हे उत्तम दाता, हमें तेज प्रदान करो।
english: Abundant, O Indra, O hundred-powered one, is the gift of your plentiful bounty; so, O all-seeing one, good giver, grant us splendour.
notes: vibhoṣṭa = vibhoḥ te (te > ta before indra). viśvacarṣaṇe may also be 'lord of all peoples'. maṃhaya 'grant, bestow'.

hindi: हे उज्ज्वल उषा, तुम्हारे (आने पर) पंखों वाले पक्षी, दोपाये और चौपाये, ऋतुओं के क्रम से द्युलोक के छोरों से आगे बढ़ चले हैं।
english: O bright one, at your (coming) the winged birds, the two-footed and the four-footed, O Dawn, have gone forth following the seasons from the ends of heaven.
notes: The sentence is taken as: vayaḥ patatriṇaḥ ... pra āran ('the winged birds ... have gone forth'). 'vayaḥ' is singular in form but collective ('birds'); the printed vayaścitte = vayaḥ cit te; 'te' (your) is taken with the dawn. prārann = pra + ārann (n doubled before the vowel ṛ); ṛtū~ranu = ṛtūn anu.

hindi: आप जो देवगण उस ओर द्युलोक के प्रकाशमान स्थान के मध्य में हैं, आपका ऋत क्या है, आपका अमृत क्या है, आपकी प्राचीन आहुति क्या है?
english: You gods yonder, who are in the middle, in the bright realm of heaven: what is your order (ṛta), what is your immortality, what is your ancient offering?

text_flags.why: possible: the Ṛgvedic parallel (1.105.5) reads kad anṛtam 'what is untruth'; printed kadamṛtam is kad amṛtam 'what is immortality'

notes: Read as printed (kad amṛtam). 'kā pratnā' also differs from the Ṛgvedic kva prattā; not applied. The question 'kat' is rendered 'what'; 'when/where' are alternatives.

hindi: हम ऋचा और साम का यजन करते हैं, जिन दोनों के द्वारा लोग कर्म करते हैं; वे दोनों सभा में शोभित होते हैं और यज्ञ को देवताओं तक पहुँचाते हैं।
english: We worship the ṛc-verse and the chant (sāman), by which two (people) perform their rites; the two shine forth in the assembly and carry the sacrifice to the gods.
notes: 'vi ... rājataḥ' is read as tmesis (vi-rāj 'shine forth'). deveṣu is rendered 'to the gods'. vakṣataḥ: 3 du. 'they two will convey' (subjunctive/future of √vah).

hindi: सब सेनाओं को जीतने वाले इन्द्र को पुरुषों ने एक साथ गढ़ा और राज्य के लिए उत्पन्न किया, बल के लिए, श्रेष्ठ के लिए, स्थिरता के लिए, चूर करने वाले, उग्र, सबसे ओजस्वी, वेगवान और शक्तिशाली को।
english: The men together fashioned and begot Indra, the surpassing conqueror of all hosts, for rule: for power, for the best, for steadiness, the crusher (?), the fierce, most vigorous, swift and impetuous one.
notes: Doubtful second line: 'vare', 'sthemani' and 'āmurīm' are not secure (āmurī taken as 'crusher'); 'kratve vare sthemani' is taken as three purpose datives/locatives. abhibhūtaram 'more overpowering' / 'surpassing conqueror'.

hindi: मैं तुम्हारे प्रथम, उग्र क्रोध पर श्रद्धा रखता हूँ, जब तुमने दस्यु को मारा और जलों को खोल दिया; जब दोनों लोक तुम्हारे पीछे दौड़े, तब हे पत्थर के धारी, पृथ्वी भी तुम्हारे बल से डर गई।
english: I put my trust in your first fury, when you slew the Dasyu, the manly one, and opened the waters; when both worlds ran after you, even the earth feared your force, O wielder of the stone.
notes: Doubtful words: naryam (taken as 'manly, of men' qualifying dasyum), bhyasāt (3 sg. 'it feared'). 'śrat te dadhāmi' = 'I place faith in you'. The two lines are one statement joined by 'when'. 'prathamāya manyave' is read as 'in your first fury'.

hindi: सब मिलकर बल से द्युलोक के स्वामी के पास आओ, जो अकेला ही जनों का अतिथि बना है। वह पुरातन, नए (पर) विजय की इच्छा करने वाला; उसकी ओर मार्गों पर अकेला ही बार-बार मुड़ता है।
english: Come together, all of you, with might to the lord of heaven, who alone has become the guest of the peoples. He, the ancient one, the new one, striving to win; along the paths he alone keeps turning to him.
notes: Doubtful second line. nūtanamājigīṣaṃ is taken as nūtanam ājigīṣam ('the new one, striving for victory'), but the grammar (case and referent) is not secure; 'taṃ vartanīr anu vāvṛte eka it' is taken as 'along the paths he alone keeps turning to him'. vāvṛta = vāvṛte with e > a before the following vowel. viśvā is taken as nom. pl. 'all'. The unit has no closing mark after line a in the input (not significant).

words.gloss: having taken hold of, relying on

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हम ये तुम्हारे हैं, हे बहुतों से स्तुत, जो तुम्हारा सहारा लेकर विचरते हैं, हे प्रभूत धन वाले; क्योंकि हे स्तुतिप्रिय, तुमसे अन्य कोई स्तुतियों को पृथ्वी की तरह ग्रहण नहीं करेगा; हमारे उस वचन का स्वागत करो।
english: These are yours, O Indra — we, O much-praised one, who go about relying on you, O abounding in wealth. For no one other than you, O lover of songs, will receive our songs, like the earth; welcome that word of ours.
notes: 'ime ta indra te vayam' is read as ime te indra, te vayam ('these are yours, Indra; we are those who ...'). Doubtful: saghat (taken as 'will take up/receive') and kṣoṇīr iva ('like the earth'); the second line's logic is therefore tentative. taddharya = tat + harya (impv. of √harya).

words.gram: pres. part. mid. m. acc. sg. √jṝ

hindi: जनों के आधार, उदार, स्तुत्य इन्द्र की ओर महान् स्तुतियाँ गूँजी हैं, जो बढ़ता हुआ, बहुतों से बुलाया गया, उत्तम स्तोत्रों से दिन-प्रतिदिन स्तुत, अमर है।
english: The great songs have sounded towards Indra, the supporter of the peoples, the bountiful and praiseworthy one, who grows strong, much invoked, immortal, praised with fine hymns day by day.
notes: The figure 3 inside maghavānamukthyā3mindraṃ marks prolongation of the chant (pluta) after ukthyā; it is not translated. The word split restores ukthyam, with the 3 as its own item. jaramāṇa: pres. part. of √jṝ 'praise'.

hindi: तुम्हारे लिए इन्द्र की ओर सब एकमत, उत्सुक, द्युलोक के प्रकाश की चाह वाली स्तुतियाँ गूँज उठी हैं; वे उदार (इन्द्र) को सहायता के लिए ऐसे गले लगाती हैं जैसे पत्नियाँ पति को, जैसे तेजस्वी युवक को।
english: Towards Indra, for you, all the united, eager hymns that long for heaven's light have sounded; they embrace the bountiful one for help, as wives embrace a husband, like a radiant young man.
notes: The Ṛgvedic parallel (10.43.1) reads ma (my) and svarvidaḥ; the printed va and svaryuvaḥ are translated as given (svaryu 'desiring svar'). 'vaḥ' is taken as 'for you (pl.)'. 'maryaṃ na śundhyum' = 'like a radiant young man'.

hindi: उस मेष को, बहुतों से बुलाए गए, ऋचा के योग्य इन्द्र को, जो धन का समुद्र है, स्तुतियों से आनन्दित करो; जिसके (दिन) द्युलोकों की तरह मनुष्य के बीच विचरते हैं, भोग के लिए उस सबसे उदार प्रेरित (इन्द्र) की स्तुति करो।
english: Delight with songs that ram, Indra, much invoked, worthy of the ṛc-hymn, the ocean of wealth; sing, for enjoyment, to the most bountiful inspired one, whose (days), like the heavens, range over mankind.
notes: Doubtful. meṣa 'ram' is kept as an epithet of Indra. In 'yasya dyāvo na vicaranti mānuṣam' the sense of dyāvaḥ ('days' or 'heavens') and the object mānuṣam are uncertain; the translation is tentative. 'bhuje' taken as 'for enjoyment'.

words.gloss: finder of the light of heaven

hindi: उस मेष को, स्वर्ग का प्रकाश पाने वाले को, भली-भाँति महिमा दो, जिसके सौ सहायक साथ-साथ उठते हैं; जैसे पुरस्कार जीतने वाले घोड़े को और पुकार पर दौड़ने वाले रथ को, वैसे ही इन्द्र को मैं उत्तम स्तोत्रों से सहायता के लिए इधर मोड़ूँ।
english: Magnify well that ram, the finder of heaven's light, whose hundred helpers rise together; like a steed (that wins) the prize, like a chariot speeding to the call, may I turn Indra hither with fine hymns for help.
notes: Doubtful words: subhuvaḥ (taken as 'helpful ones'), atyaṃ na vājaṃ havanasyadaṃ ratham (the two similes 'steed, chariot' are read as comparing Indra's coming). 'ā ... vavṛtyām' = 'may I turn hither'.

hindi: घृत से भरी, भुवनों का आश्रय, विशाल और व्यापक, मधु दुहने वाली, सुन्दर रूप वाली द्यावा-पृथिवी, वरुण के धारण-विधान से थामकर अलग-अलग रखी गई, अजर, प्रचुर वीर्य वाली।
english: Rich in ghee, the refuge of the worlds, wide and broad, yielding honey, fair of form: Heaven and Earth, propped apart by the ordinance of Varuṇa, unageing, of abundant seed.
notes: abhiśriyā is taken as a dual feminine 'resort, refuge' (doubtful). dharmaṇā: 'by the ordinance/support'. The pair is in the dual throughout.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, जब तुमने उषा की तरह दोनों लोकों को भर दिया — तुम्हें, जो महान् हो, महान् जनों के और मनुष्यों के सम्राट् हो — तब देवी माता ने तुम्हें जन्म दिया, कल्याणी माता ने तुम्हें जन्म दिया।
english: When, O Indra, you filled both worlds like the dawn — you, the great one, the supreme ruler of the great ones and of the peoples — the goddess mother bore you, the auspicious mother bore you.
notes: Three printed lines (a, b, c) are kept as one unit as in the edition. The syntax runs across the lines: 'when you filled ... — you, great — the mother bore (you)'. 'āpaprāthoṣā' = āpaprātha + uṣāḥ (the form āpaprātha 'you filled' is from ā-√prā). mahīnām is taken as 'of the great ones' (or 'of the earths').

words.gloss: those pregnant with the dark one (?)
with the thunderbolt in the right hand

hindi: प्रसन्न करने वाले के लिए अन्न से भरा वचन गाओ, जिसने ऋजिश्वा के साथ काले (कृष्ण) की गर्भवती (स्त्रियों) को मार निकाला; सहायता चाहने वाले हम मित्रता के लिए उस वृषभ को, दाहिने हाथ में वज्र रखने वाले, मरुतों वाले को पुकारें।
english: Sing a food-rich word to the exhilarating one, who with Ṛjiśvan struck out those pregnant with the dark one (?); desiring help, may we call, for friendship, the bull, with the thunderbolt in his right hand, accompanied by the Maruts.
notes: Doubtful: kṛṣṇagarbhāḥ ('those pregnant with Kṛṣṇa / the black ones' wombs') is kept literal; no story is imported. nirahann = niḥ + ahan (n doubled before ṛ). Ṛjiśvan is kept as a name. pitumat 'rich in food/nourishment'.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, निचोड़े हुए सोमों में तुम अपने स्तुत्य संकल्प (बल) को शुद्ध करते हो; वह बढ़ाने वाली कुशलता के लिए जाना जाता है, क्योंकि वह महान् है।
english: O Indra, in the pressed Soma-offerings you purify your praiseworthy purpose; he is known for his thriving skill, for he is great.
notes: Doubtful second line: vide is taken as 3 sg. 'is known'; vṛdhasya dakṣasya as genitives 'of the thriving skill'; the Ṛgvedic wording and the exact construction are not checked. kratu = purpose/power. The speaker shifts from 'you' to 'he' (Indra).

hindi: उस बहुतों से बुलाए गए और बहुतों से स्तुत (इन्द्र) के लिए आगे गाओ; शक्तिशाली इन्द्र को गीतों से सम्मानित करो।
english: Sing forth to him, the much invoked, the much praised; honour mighty Indra with songs.

hindi: हे पत्थर के धारी, हम तुम्हारे उस आनन्ददायक रस की स्तुति करते हैं, जो बलशाली है, संग्रामों में विजयी है, लोक (स्थान) बनाने वाला है और हरे (पीले) रंग की शोभा वाला है।
english: We praise for you, O wielder of the stone, that exhilarating draught, virile and victorious in the contests, the maker of space, splendid with the tawny ones.
notes: Doubtful: pṛkṣu (taken as 'in contests'; also 'in feasts'), lokakṛtnu 'making room/space', hariśriyam 'splendid with the tawny (horses or Soma)'.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, चाहे विष्णु में सोम के साथ, चाहे आप्त्य त्रित के पास, चाहे मरुतों के बीच तुम आनन्दित होते हो — बूँदों के साथ आनन्दित होते हो।
english: Whether, O Indra, you rejoice with the Soma in Viṣṇu, or with Trita Āptya, or among the Maruts, you rejoice together with the drops.
notes: viṣṇavi is taken as locative 'in/with Viṣṇu'; trita = trite. The verb mandase of the second line serves the whole sentence; somam is the Soma with which Indra rejoices.

hindi: हे अध्वर्यु, शहद से भी अधिक मादक सोम-रस को उँडेलो; इस प्रकार ही वीर सदा बढ़ने वाला कहकर स्तुत होता है।
english: Pour in, O adhvaryu priest, the juice that is more intoxicating than honey; thus indeed the hero is praised, ever-growing.
notes: edu = ā id u. madintaram is taken with andhasaḥ ('more intoxicating (draught) of the juice'); the unstated object is the Soma. sadāvṛdhaḥ 'ever-increasing'.

hindi: इन्द्र के लिए सोम-बिन्दु उँडेलो; वह सोम का मधुर रस पिए; वह अपनी महिमा से दानों को आगे प्रेरित करता है।
english: Pour the drop for Indra; may he drink the sweet Soma-draught; by his greatness he sets bounties in motion.
notes: endumindrāya = ā indum indrāya. 'pra codayate' is taken as 'sets forth (impels) bounties'.

hindi: आओ, मित्रो, अब हम इन्द्र की स्तुति करें, जो स्तुति के योग्य वीर है, जो अकेला ही सब जनों पर प्रबल है।
english: Come, friends, let us now praise Indra, the hero worthy of praise, who alone prevails over all the peoples.
notes: 'abhi ... asti' is taken as 'prevails over'. See verse 350 for the same opening words.

hindi: इन्द्र के लिए साम गाओ; उस प्रेरित, महान् के लिए महान् (साम) गाओ; प्रार्थना रचने वाले, ज्ञानी और प्रशंसनीय के लिए।
english: Sing a chant (sāman) for Indra; for the inspired, the great one, sing the great (chant); for the maker of prayer, the wise, the admirable.
notes: bṛhat may name the Bṛhat chant (sāman) or simply mean 'the great (chant)'; rendered 'the great (chant)'. brahmakṛte 'maker of prayer' (or 'of sacred speech').

hindi: जो अकेला ही देने वाले मनुष्य को धन बाँटता है, वह स्वामी, अप्रतिरोध्य इन्द्र ही है।
english: He who alone apportions wealth to the mortal who gives worship, the master, the irresistible one: it is Indra indeed.
notes: aṅga 'indeed' (a particle of emphasis, also 'O dear one'). dāśuṣe 'who offers/gives (to the gods)'.

words.gloss: to the wielder of the thunderbolt

hindi: हे मित्रो, हम वज्रधारी इन्द्र के लिए प्रार्थना करते हैं; मैं तुम्हारे लिए उस सबसे वीर, साहसी की भली-भाँति स्तुति करता हूँ।
english: O friends, we pray for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt; I praise well for you the most manly, the bold one.
notes: 'ā śiṣāmahe brahma' is rendered 'we pray (with) prayer for Indra' in a loose sense; the object brahma is taken as 'prayer'. The second line shifts to the singular 'I'.
